listing.name: DKR-R
listing.summary: Diddy Kong Racing through an upstream-owned DKR-R launcher that you manage.

steps.title: Open the Linux AppImage
steps.instruction: Choose the official x86-64, ARM64 or Steam Deck package for your device. Mark the AppImage executable and open it. Check the upstream platform guide for your release’s Vulkan and system-library requirements.

steps.title: Add your original game
steps.instruction: In Play, choose Add a ROM and select your own clean US v1.0 or US Rev A/v1.1 original. Some older mods need US v1.0 when you install them.

warnings: Use DKR-R’s upstream launcher and update instructions for your Linux copy. Back up the active profile before replacing the package or switching profile locations.

references.title: Find your DKR-R profile
references.instruction: Linux normally uses $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dkr-port or ~/.config/dkr-port. Portable mode uses dkr-runtime-data beside the application. Changing modes selects a different profile on the next launch. Use DKR-R’s Save Manager to export progress and back up your settings and installed content separately.

presentation.manual_preparation: Extract the complete official Windows package into a folder you manage outside the Portcove library. Use upstream’s launcher to select your own supported Diddy Kong Racing original. Select the top-level DKR-R.exe with that release folder as its working directory; leave libexec and helpers intact. Optional --rom and --config arguments belong to your selected upstream profile. DKR-R or you manage runtime updates, saves, settings and backups. Portcove only registers, launches and removes the registration. Existing Portcove-managed installations keep their retained contracts; do not move their files into this route.
